Definition: an olive (as yielding illuminating oil), the tree, the branch or the berry
BiblicalUsage: Zayith is the olive, the tree and its fruit and its oil, and it runs through the whole Bible. The dove brings Noah an olive leaf, the first sign that the waters have gone down, and the tabernacle lamps burn on pure beaten olive oil. Zechariah sees two olive trees feeding the lampstand with oil, and the Psalmist says the righteous man is like a green olive tree in the house of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the olive is a picture of life that keeps going when everything else is stripped bare, because the tree lives for centuries and bears fruit after the flood. Its oil lights the lamp, anoints the king, and heals the wound, and that is no accident. My position is that God chose the olive on purpose: the life He gives endures, and it gives light to others.
